svg.title: Allocate Acquisition Capital Without Calling It Revenue
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation-comparison; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Acquisition Capital Without Calling It Revenue; subtitle: Four buckets across $150,000, $600,000, and $2,000,000 startup plans.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: All amounts are USD. Numeric stage values describe the $600,000 reference stack; each stage also identifies the corresponding floor and ceiling allocations. These are alternative capital plans, not additive funding rounds and not mappings to the three annual revenue scenarios. Reserves and acquisition principal are balance-sheet uses, not recognized royalty or trading revenue.; caption: Floor: $100,000 + $20,000 + $18,000 + $12,000 = $150,000. Reference: $450,000 + $60,000 + $60,000 + $30,000 = $600,000. Ceiling: $1,600,000 + $160,000 + $180,000 + $60,000 = $2,000,000.; stages: label: Fund acquired interests and documented purchase basis; value: $450,000 reference allocation for mineral acquisition principal; numeric value: 450000.0; detail: Floor allocation is $100,000; ceiling allocation is $1,600,000. Deploy only against documented asset underwriting and closing evidence. Track basis by interest so later disposal proceeds do not inflate recognized rights-trading gains.; label: Reserve transaction-specific diligence and closing capital; value: $60,000 reference allocation for diligence and closing; numeric value: 60000.0; detail: Floor allocation is $20,000; ceiling allocation is $160,000. Cover title examination, engineering, recording, and instrument preparation. Separate capitalized acquisition costs from expensed failed-deal work; do not charge the same invoice twice.; label: Hold operating liquidity against delayed first receipts; value: $60,000 reference allocation for protected operating liquidity; numeric value: 60000.0; detail: Floor allocation is $18,000; ceiling allocation is $180,000. At selected monthly burns of $1,000, $2,500, and $7,500 respectively, these fund 18, 24, and 24 months. The floor plan needs another $6,000 or equivalent reductions if first receipts take 24 months.; label: Provision startup systems and controlled contingency cash; value: $30,000 reference allocation for setup and contingency; numeric value: 30000.0; detail: Floor allocation is $12,000; ceiling allocation is $60,000. Cover initial data access, secure document storage, account setup, and a remaining contingency balance. Contingency can extend runway only to the extent it remains unspent.

text.title: Fund acquired interests and documented purchase basis

rect.title: label: Fund acquired interests and documented purchase basis; numeric value: 450000.0; value: $450,000 reference allocation for mineral acquisition principal; detail: Floor allocation is $100,000; ceiling allocation is $1,600,000. Deploy only against documented asset underwriting and closing evidence. Track basis by interest so later disposal proceeds do not inflate recognized rights-trading gains.

text.title: Reserve transaction-specific diligence and closing capital

rect.title: label: Reserve transaction-specific diligence and closing capital; numeric value: 60000.0; value: $60,000 reference allocation for diligence and closing; detail: Floor allocation is $20,000; ceiling allocation is $160,000. Cover title examination, engineering, recording, and instrument preparation. Separate capitalized acquisition costs from expensed failed-deal work; do not charge the same invoice twice.

text.title: Hold operating liquidity against delayed first receipts

rect.title: label: Hold operating liquidity against delayed first receipts; numeric value: 60000.0; value: $60,000 reference allocation for protected operating liquidity; detail: Floor allocation is $18,000; ceiling allocation is $180,000. At selected monthly burns of $1,000, $2,500, and $7,500 respectively, these fund 18, 24, and 24 months. The floor plan needs another $6,000 or equivalent reductions if first receipts take 24 months.
